prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study sought to determine how the shape of pressure waves in the brain changes after a specific saline injection is used to lower high pressure.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The research involved ten patients who had suffered brain trauma and were experiencing dangerously high pressure inside their skulls.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The saline injections caused a temporary drop in the overall pressure and in the measured wave features.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Some wave features varied more between different patients, while others fluctuated more within the same patient over time.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Patients who started with higher pressure tended to see a bigger drop in certain wave features after the treatment.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The starting shape of the waves did not help predict how much the pressure would fall once the starting pressure level was taken into account.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The shape of the pressure waves is affected by pressure changes but still shows significant differences from one person to another.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: One specific wave feature, the pulse amplitude, is mainly determined by the level of pressure in the skull.
facts.subject: humans
